gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Bushnell's own Core trail-camera manual advises against rechargeable NiMH AA cells: 'NiMh Rechargeable batteries are not recommended, as the lower voltage they produce can cause operational issues.' The same manual recommends 'a full set of new lithium AA (Energizer® brand) or alkaline AA batteries.'
standout_why: I compared four pages. Cam & Canopy's best non-cellular list (cited by ChatGPT) ties long battery-life estimates to Energizer lithium and says the Spec Ops HP5 lists rechargeable AAs as supported. It never gives a cell voltage or warns about NiMH. TrailCamSetup says only 'Lithium AA batteries are worth the extra cost in cold weather.' MyWildlifeCam says '8 AA' and never names a battery chemistry. The cited Digital Camera World S-4K review came back with only its headline, so I couldn't check it. None of these pages says the camera maker advises against 1.2 V NiMH. That warning matters to a shopper whose SD-only camera has to run for months on AA cells.
decides: The camera pick stays the same, but the power plan changes. An SD-only camera depends entirely on its AA set, and Bushnell says NiMH cells (eneloop, Tenergy) can cause operational issues because of their lower voltage. The page should tell the shopper to use 1.5 V lithium cells: Energizer lithium AAs per Bushnell's manual, or possibly 1.5 V regulated rechargeables such as the XTAR AA that Dealectric lists, though I found no maker statement approving those. NiMH packs should not be the default. One exception: I could open this warning only in the manual for the older Core line (119936C/119938C/119975C/119977C). I could not read the text of the current S-4K/DS-4K manual, so the page must not quote the warning as S-4K wording. On a separate note, the GardePro E5 2.0 cost $63.99 on GardePro's US store today, below the $79.99 card ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: Maker guidance on NiMH rechargeable AAs
findings.value: Not recommended: 'NiMh Rechargeable batteries are not recommended, as the lower voltage they produce can cause operational issues.'
findings.note: This is Bushnell's manual for the earlier Core line, not the S-4K/DS-4K (119949C/119987C). I couldn't extract text from the S-4K/DS-4K PDF (Adorama BS119987C.pdf).

findings.label: Recommended batteries
findings.value: 6 AA; 'a full set of new lithium AA (Energizer® brand) or alkaline AA batteries'
findings.note: The same page says 'other external power supplies should not be used'. It also limits the old Core line to SD/SDHC cards of 32 GB maximum, which does not carry over to the 4K models.

findings.label: Battery life caveat
findings.value: 'Battery life will vary with operating temperature and the number of images taken over time'; 'Bushnell recommends using Energizer® Lithium AA batteries in your Core Trail Camera model to obtain maximum battery life.'
findings.source_title: Bushnell Core Instruction Manual, Troubleshooting/FAQ page 20 (ManualsLib)
